title: MCP Fundamentals: Stateless Requests and JSON-RPC
service: MCPCore: the stateless core of a small MCP notes server: request builders, a dispatcher, a SQLite transcript, the request lifecycle checks, a stateless tracer and nested capability matching

parts.lesson_anchor: The Problem; Required request metadata; Exercises 1, 2, 3 and 5; code/main.py make_request, request_meta and dispatch
planted_bugs: make_request writes _meta into the caller's params dict, so two requests built from the same params share one _meta (a deepcopy of the finished request still leaves _meta in the caller's dict); the failure surfaces two calls later, as the server answering a 2027-01-01 request instead of refusing it with -32022
request_meta puts the module-level NO_CAPABILITIES dict into every request that passes no capabilities, so a capability one caller adds to its own request appears in every later request
NotesServer.dispatch remembers the last declared capabilities and fills them into a request that has none (inferring from an earlier request, the legacy connection-scoped habit)
tools/list returns tools in registration order, so reversing the registry changes the result (exercise 3)
tools/call sorts the whole registry and scans it on every call
parts.timing_assert: 20000 tools registered in shuffled order, 500 tools/call requests timed after gc.collect(), under 0.04 s. Measured here: the sort-and-scan lookup takes 1.4-2.4 s (36x the limit or more), the dict index 0.4-1.2 ms (34x under it or more); a plain linear scan without the sort takes 65-190 ms and fails too
parts.overfix_guard: a request without capabilities is still -32602 when missing capabilities are read as {} (in validate_request or by setdefault in dispatch); a request without clientInfo stays valid when every _meta key is made required; a tool registered after construction is callable and listed, which rules out an index built once in __init__ and a cached sorted listing

parts.lesson_anchor: JSON-RPC envelopes (the id correlates one response; a notification has no id); Ship It skill: preserve the original transcript
parts.exactness: every raw line round-trips byte for byte across close and reopen (a trailing \r, a \u00e9 escape, a line that is not valid UTF-8), and ids come back with their JSON type: 7 and "7" stay apart, an id-null error stays apart from an id-less notification (NO_ID), and 2**64 + 1 stays exact

parts.lesson_anchor: One request lifecycle, step 6 (check required capabilities); Required request metadata (the client capabilities object)

deviations: Part 1: a fifth bug, make_request reusing the caller's params dict, is added so that the first failure surfaces at the server's version check, two calls from its root cause; the four suggested bugs and both suggested guards stay, and a third guard requires tools registered after construction to be callable and listed. The timing uses 20000 tools registered in shuffled order and 500 calls instead of 3000 x 3000, so that the per-call sort and a plain linear scan both fail while a dict index passes with margin on a loaded machine.

Part 3: -32021 moves into Part 5's end-to-end checks, because its data is exactly what Part 5 computes and Part 3 must pass without Part 5. check_request keeps the step-6 slot in its docstring; Part 3 covers -32700, -32600, -32602, -32020, -32022, -32601 and notifications, which are never answered outside HTTP and are checked like requests over HTTP.

Part 4: the stream carries parsed messages without a direction. An unanswered or doubly answered response gets the kind orphan and the method ?. Era rules follow the lesson's Ship It skill (-32020, -32021 and -32022 are modern evidence; initialize, its result and notifications/initialized are legacy) rather than code/main.py's trace_message, which labels every error unknown and every result without resultType legacy.
Part 5: matching is wired into check_request through a requirement table (method to nested capability object), so the part also checks where -32021 sits in the lifecycle.

Facts used beyond docs/en.md, all from this phase: -32700 with a null id (lessons 07 and 09); the header names MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name, Mcp-Name mirroring params.uri for resources/read, and a missing header being -32020 (lesson 09); -32021 Missing Required Client Capability with data.requiredCapabilities and the tasks extension requirement (lessons 11, 13, 14, 15 and 23); Mcp-Name mirroring params.taskId for tasks methods (lesson 13); an unknown tool name as a JSON-RPC error (lesson 28); a notification sent over HTTP checked like a request before it is accepted, an error for it carrying a null id, and an accepted one getting no response (lesson 09); a tasks result with resultType task (lesson 13).

Traps that would otherwise appear a third time in this phase are left out: a body that is not valid UTF-8 (lessons 07 and 09), ids conflated by str() (lesson 08's pending table and this pack's Part 2, which still keeps 7 and "7" apart in storage; the tracer's ids never collide under str()), and id 0 taken for a notification (lessons 07 and 14; the interviewer asks about it instead).
